info.name: Auth
info.description:
Session and password endpoints.

## Response envelope
Every endpoint answers with the same wrapper:
```json
{ "success": true, "statusCode": 200, "message": "...", "data": { } }
```
Read your payload from `data`. On failure `success` is `false` and `message` holds the text to show the user.

## Tokens
There are two kinds of bearer token and they are NOT interchangeable:

| Token | Comes from | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Session token | `POST /auth/login` | every `@Auth()` route |
| Purpose token | forget-password / register flows | only the next step of that same flow |

A purpose token lasts 10 minutes and works for exactly one flow step. Sending a session token where a purpose token is expected returns 401.

request.description:
Sign in and receive a session token.

**Body**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| email | string | yes | |
| password | string | yes | |
| isRememberMe | boolean | no | `true` makes the token last 30 days instead of 7 |

**Returns**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 200,
  "message": "User logged in successfully",
  "data": {
    "token": "eyJhbGci...",
    "user": {
      "id": 13,
      "email": "admin@gmail.com",
      "name": "Admin",
      "phone": "",
      "role": "superAdmin",
      "isEmailVerified": true
    }
  }
}
```

**Errors**
| Status | message | What to show |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | Invalid credentials | Wrong email or password — the same message for both, on purpose, so nobody can discover which emails exist |
| 403 | Please verify your email before logging in. | Send them to the OTP screen; call `POST /users/resend-email-otp` to get a fresh code |

**Note on `role`:** this is the platform role only — `user` or `superAdmin`. Commissioner and Team Owner are per-league and do not appear here.

The test script stores `data.token` into the `accessToken` variable, so every protected request below works straight after this one.

The signed-in user, read fresh from the database.

**Auth:** session token.

Use this on app start to restore the session: if it returns 200 the stored token is still good, if it returns 401 send the user back to login.

**Returns** the same `user` object that login returns.

Step 1 of 3. Emails a 6-digit OTP and returns the purpose token for step 2.

**Body:** `{ "email": "..." }`

**Returns**
```json
{ "data": { "token": "eyJhbGci..." } }
```
Keep this token in memory — step 2 needs it as a bearer token.

**Errors**
| Status | message |
|---|---|
| 404 | This account does not exist. |

Unverified accounts are rejected here too, so one email can never have a registration OTP and a reset OTP pending at the same time.

The email is sent **after** the response, so this returns immediately. In development the OTP is also printed to the server terminal:
```
[OtpService] OTP for you@example.com: 123456
```

The test script saves the token as `forgetToken`.

Step 2 of 3. Checks the OTP and hands back a second purpose token for the actual password change.

**Auth:** the `forgetToken` from step 1.

**Body:** `{ "otp": "123456" }` — the OTP is **6 digits**.

**Returns**
```json
{ "data": { "token": "eyJhbGci..." } }
```

**Errors**
| Status | message |
|---|---|
| 404 | OTP not found! |
| 400 | OTP has expired |
| 400 | Wrong OTP |
| 401 | Invalid or expired token |

The OTP is single use: a successful check deletes it, so going back and resubmitting the same code fails with `OTP not found!`.

The test script saves the new token as `resetToken`.

Sends a fresh forget-password OTP. No body.

**Auth:** the `forgetToken` from step 1 — the same token stays valid.

Wire this to the "Didn't receive code? Resend" link on the OTP screen.

The old OTP is replaced, so only the newest code works.

Step 3 of 3. Sets the new password.

**Auth:** the `resetToken` from step 2 — **not** the step 1 token.

**Body**
| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| password | string | at least 6 characters |
| confirmPassword | string | must match `password` |

**Errors**
| Status | message |
|---|---|
| 400 | Passwords do not match |
| 401 | Invalid or expired token |

After this the user signs in normally with the new password.

Changes the password of a user who is already signed in. This is the Settings screen, not the forgotten-password flow.

**Auth:** session token.

**Body**
| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| oldPassword | string | the current password |
| newPassword | string | at least 6 characters |
| confirmPassword | string | must match `newPassword` |

**Errors**
| Status | message |
|---|---|
| 401 | Old password is incorrect |
| 400 | Passwords do not match |
